prompt: In the beginning, computer systems were constrained by memory rather than compute.
The primary bottleneck in modern large language model decoding on commodity hardware is memory bandwidth.
Singular value decomposition provides an optimal low-rank matrix approximation under the Frobenius norm.
When paging model weights from secondary storage, NVMe read latency and sequential bandwidth determine throughput.
Adaptive layer skipping allows models to dynamically allocate compute based on token complexity.
A working set policy tracks temporal locality of references across autoregressive decoding steps.
Residual connections in transformer architectures facilitate gradient flow during training.
Evaluating language models on commodity CPUs requires balancing quality against latency and peak memory footprint.
